quote: I'm not gonna put it on my roof.
stewart_read: Customer's ground-mount-on-a-future-structure plan is outside the standard verify flow; rep should have flagged this as a hold-for-specialist case rather than trying to keep running the roof script.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's clarifying question ('ground mounted installation then specifically?') could be read as competent on-the-fly adaptation rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: When roof-mount is explicitly rejected, pivot immediately to capturing the alternative structure's details and set expectations that pricing needs those specifics — don't keep re-anchoring to roof.

quote: I need to know how much it's gonna cost, then I'll know what direction to go.
stewart_read: This is a textbook price-before-design ask; the canonical response redirects to grabbing info for a real design, but the rep instead just explains why pricing isn't possible yet, leaving the customer without a next step.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally stalling because the lead genuinely can't be priced (structure unbuilt) — a legitimate constraint, not a scripting failure.
coaching_implication: Even when a real design isn't possible yet, redirect_to_design language ('once we know the structure specs we can build you real numbers') keeps momentum instead of open-ended deferral.

quote: I just need some prices so I know which way to go.
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the same price-first ask; rep again explains the sizing/space logic rather than converting it into a design-capture commitment or locked follow-up.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be avoiding false hope on price given the structure doesn't exist yet — a defensible caution.
coaching_implication: Use the repeated price ask as leverage: 'let's lock a callback date so the moment your structure's built, we can get you real numbers fast' ties urgency to the customer's own stated need.

quote: I'm not gonna have anybody to install it. I'm only install it myself.
stewart_read: Self-install almost certainly disqualifies this lead from Ion's model (professional install, warranty, financing all assume Ion installs), but the rep responds with uncertainty rather than a clear answer.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be improvising honestly given no schema guidance for DIY installs, which is a legitimate knowledge gap rather than an execution failure.
coaching_implication: Escalate self-install requests to a manager/checklist rather than guessing live — 'let me check with my team on our self-install policy and follow up' preserves the lead without overpromising.

quote: okay. Well, maybe I can try calling back some other time then.
stewart_read: Call ends with no locked date/time, no 'is that fair' handshake, and no owned next step — just a vague future callback.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the genuine bad connection and unresolved DQ-adjacent scenario, an open-ended exit may be the pragmatic choice over forcing a hard date.
coaching_implication: Even on a messy call, lock a specific day/time for the callback rather than 'some other time' — it protects the pipeline and gives the rep a concrete next action.

quote: Yeah. I'm interested in this call, but most of them, I'm not interested.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly distinguishes this call as one he's actually interested in, a positive signal the rep doesn't leverage to re-engage or lock a real next step.
coaching_implication: When a customer volunteers genuine interest amid skepticism about other calls, that's the moment to pin down a concrete callback time, not let the call drift into small talk.
